title: Operator turn record, version 1
description: What one operator turn IS, independent of who produced it and who reads it. Derived from 159 records produced by the Emacs implementation and checked against all of them; not designed from one consumer's needs. A second implementation conforms to this rather than to the first implementation.

source_text.description: The text every offset in this record indexes. NOT necessarily what the operator typed: if the turn carried quoted material, source_text is the text with each quoted block replaced by the token QUOTE, and original_text holds what was typed. Both are kept because a turn has two readers who need different things -- an interpreter must not mistake quoted words for the operator's own, and a display must show what was on screen. Designing this field around either reader alone is the mistake this seam was built after.

original_text.description: What the operator actually typed, present when it differs from source_text.

quotes.description: The elided blocks, in the order their QUOTE tokens appear in source_text.

offset_unit.description: Stated rather than assumed. A UTF-16 client (JavaScript) and a codepoint client (Python, Emacs) disagree on any turn containing an emoji or CJK, and the disagreement is silent. Convert at your boundary; do not change this constant.

text.description: Must equal source_text[start:end]. This is the conformance test that matters: an implementation whose splitter disagrees will fail here rather than silently produce misaligned annotations.

method.description: How this cue was found, e.g. literal-phrase. Recorded so a later reader can tell a matched convention from a judgement.

unmatched.description: Sentences carrying no cue. Kept as an explicit list rather than inferred, so 'nothing matched' is distinguishable from 'nothing ran'.

surface.description: Where the turn arrived from: typed, dictated, relayed. Absent in records written before the field existed.

analysis_status.description: requested means dispatched and not yet answered. refused and failed are distinct from requested on purpose: a delegate that declined and a delegate that is busy left the same state until 2026-09-24, and 152 records accumulated with no reason attached to any of them.

analysis_dispatch.description: The job the dispatch created, so the outcome can be traced. A fire-and-forget caller that does not record this cannot tell a refusal from a busy seat.
